messages:
oncall-bot: Paging: High error rate + latency spike for /v1/generate (us-west-2). CPU/latency alerts firing, customer 42 reporting degraded responses. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/1832 - paging eng-oncall :rotating_light:

maya: ACKed. I'm looking at service/runtime - seeing KV cache evictions rapidly increasing and a correlated jump in tail-latency around 18:31 UTC.

jordan: I rolled the batch-config change at 18:20 in the runtime rollout (small tweak to continuous batch heuristics). Might be related: lowered continuous_batch_window_ms from 80 -> 20 for faster flushes and increased max_batch_size default in config.

maya: Heap growth + GC pauses match the time of that rollout. KV cache keys spiking -> more memory churn. Getting OOM-kill risk on a couple pods. Logs show lots of: `kv_cache: page_faults=XXXXX` and `kv_persistence.write_back_queue` backlog.

lee: Customer 42 on Dedicated hit 503s for ~7m. Support already pinged them and created incident ticket INC-4621. They saw partial outputs truncated, not full failures.

jordan: rolling back the config to previous batch params is the fastest mitigation. Can someone flip the flag? It's gated by feature-flag service `batch.behavior.v2`.

siva: On it. I'll gate a canary rollback first (5% traffic) then widen. Using the console to toggle.

deploy-bot: deploy:rollback request accepted for config: runtime/batch-config@prod. Initiated canary rollback to 5% at 18:38 UTC. (id: rb-1832001111-01)

maya: Nice. While canary goes we should also apply a per-customer override for high-traffic tenants (cust 42 + 17) to pin them to safer batch defaults so they don't see flapping. Command to set override: ```
# set per-customer batch override
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/api/override \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEY" \
  -d '{"flag":"batch.behavior.v2","customer":"42","value":"legacy"}'
```

siva: Applied per-customer override for 42 and 17 -> confirmed. hooks show override active on edge-router: `flag_override(batch.behavior.v2)=legacy`

maya: Canary rollback metrics: first canary pod shows latency dropping and cache page_faults returning to baseline within 90s. No new OOMs on that host.

jordan: I recommend widening to 25% next to validate cross-az behavior, then 100% if stable. Also queuing a config hotfix to avoid future autoscaling thrash: reduce max_batch_size cap from 1024 -> 512 and add backpressure on kv_persistence queue. Draft patch: ```
# runtime batch-config snippet
continuous_batch_window_ms: 80
default_max_batch_size: 512
kv_persistence_backpressure_threshold: 0.65
```

lee: I'll update incident ticket with customer impact and ETA. Telling cust 42: mitigations in progress, temporary per-cust setting applied, full rollback underway.

siva: Widened canary to 25% at 18:44 UTC. Observing metrics...

maya: 25% looks good. Memory and tail-latency trending down across AZs. No new error spikes. Rolling to 100% now.

deploy-bot: rollout:rb-1832001111-01 progressed to 100% at 18:48 UTC. All runtime nodes now using rolled-back batch-behavior.v1.

jordan: Patch queued to main branch and schedule for hotfix deploy in 30m to make change permanent (no longer rely on flag). I'll include extra logging around kv write_backs.

maya: Postmortem checklist: - Confirm no residual OOMs - Validate per-cust overrides are cleared after hotfix - Add alert for rapid KV page_fault growth (new detector) - Add playbook steps for immediate per-cust overrides and safe-canary thresholds.

lee: Customer 42 responded: "Thanks, latency improved — will monitor." Marking impact as degraded performance, not data loss.

maya: Good. Keeping this thread open for the hotfix deploy results. If anything regresses we escalate back to rollback/disable. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied, rollback + per-customer overrides in place, monitor for 30m then transition to followup. Incident severity downgraded to Sev-2 at 19:05 UTC.
